item.title: HTML5 chord-only pairs align with lyrics instead of chord line
item.justification: When a chord-lyric pair has an empty lyric span (chord-only, e.g., trailing [Am] [Em] at the end of a line), the HTML5 output aligns the chord with the lyric baseline instead of the chord line. This misalignment makes chord-only entries drop to the lyric line and disrupts the chord row alignment.

tasks.task: Reproduce chord-only alignment behavior in HTML5 output and capture the HTML/CSS for cp-chord-lyric-pair cp-chord-only.
Identify the CSS/layout rule that aligns chord-only pairs to the lyric baseline instead of the chord line.
Fix chord-only alignment so chords remain on the chord line (e.g., adjust display/vertical-align for cp-chord-only).
Add regression coverage for chord-only alignment in HTML5 output.

test.description: HTML5 chord-only pair alignment.
test.assertions: Chord-only pairs remain aligned with the chord line and do not drop to the lyric baseline.

r.observations: Added flex-start alignment for chord-only pairs in HTML5 and paged CSS and created t/192_html5_chord_only_align.t; MANIFEST updated, but the extended test run was interrupted (exit 130) before completion.
r.lessons-learned: Chord-only alignment depends on consistent flex item alignment across both standard and paged CSS templates.

item.title: HTML5 configurable song page breaks
item.justification: HTML5 paged output needs a configurable way to force page breaks before or after each song so users can control song separation in print layouts without manual CSS edits.

tasks.task: Define HTML5 config keys for song page breaks (before/after/both/none) and update config schema/defaults.
Apply the config in the HTML5 song wrapper (paged output) with CSS classes or inline styles.
Add or update documentation for the new HTML5 page break setting.
Add regression tests for page-break before/after song rendering in HTML5 paged output.

test.description: HTML5 song page-break configuration.
test.assertions: Configured before/after page-breaks appear on the song container in paged output.

r.observations: Paged song breaks now insert dedicated break elements between songs and only apply after-break classes on song wrappers, with tests and docs updated accordingly.
r.lessons-learned: Dedicated break elements avoid leading blank pages and behave more consistently than relying on wrapper break-before.

item.title: HTML5 minimal paged output bundle with externalized CSS
item.justification: To validate item 19 page-break behavior with the smallest possible surface area, create an absolute minimal HTML5 paged output test: no TOC, minimal stylesheets, and only a page-break section. Templates should emit separate CSS files (split between page/structure/layout and content such as fonts/images), and output should be a folder containing the HTML plus the required CSS files.

tasks.task: Define a minimal HTML5 paged template variant that renders only the page-break section (no TOC) for deterministic tests.
Split HTML5 paged stylesheets into external CSS files, separating page/structure/layout from content (fonts, images) and update templates to link them.
Update HTML5 output to emit a folder bundle (HTML file + referenced CSS assets) for the minimal paged variant.
Add a minimal regression test that asserts the bundle structure, linked CSS files, and page-break section output.

test.description: Minimal HTML5 paged bundle output with externalized CSS.
test.assertions: Output creates a folder with HTML + CSS files, omits TOC, and includes the page-break section.

r.observations: Added a minimal paged bundle mode that writes a folder with HTML plus split layout/content CSS, and introduced a minimal paged songbook template that omits TOC. Implemented a focused regression test; running make refreshed Config/Data.pm and Config.pod after the config changes.
r.lessons-learned: Bundle output should be written directly by the backend to avoid the standard single-file output path.

item.title: HTML5 output includes excessive empty lines
item.justification: HTML5 output currently emits many unnecessary blank lines, making the generated HTML harder to diff, review, and post-process. The output should be condensed to avoid redundant empty lines while preserving semantic formatting.

tasks.task: Identify the HTML5 template/output paths that introduce redundant blank lines in generated HTML.
Condense HTML5 output by trimming or normalizing repeated blank lines without changing semantic output.
Add regression coverage that asserts HTML5 output does not contain runs of unnecessary empty lines.

test.description: HTML5 output blank line normalization.
test.assertions: Generated HTML does not contain redundant consecutive empty lines.

r.observations: HTML5 output now normalizes multiple blank lines and returns newline-free line arrays to avoid doubled spacing.
r.lessons-learned: Normalize HTML output before line splitting to prevent writer joins from reintroducing extra whitespace.

item.title: Remove gray background from HTML5 paged output
item.justification: HTML5 paged output currently applies a gray background in the screen preview styles. Switch it to white or remove the background to simplify the default visual presentation.

tasks.task: Identify where the HTML5 paged background color is set for screen output.
Update the paged screen styles to use white or remove the background setting.
Add regression coverage to confirm the paged screen background is no longer gray.

test.assertions: Paged HTML5 screen styles no longer apply a gray background.

r.observations: Paged screen preview styles now use a white background and the regression test validates the change.
r.lessons-learned: Keeping preview styles aligned with print defaults avoids visual surprises.

item.title: Consolidate HTML5 paged templates and external CSS split
item.justification: Minimal paged output now works, but the template set is fragmented. Refactor the paged templates to use external stylesheets split into layout/content, merge templates where possible to reduce complexity, remove obsolete files, and move minimal config templates to testing. Remove the minimal template entry from config to keep the production configuration lean.

Remove obsolete paged template files and update references accordingly.

r.observations: Consolidated paged CSS into shared layout/content templates, updated bundle output to always externalize CSS, moved minimal templates into testing, and refreshed config docs and tests.
r.lessons-learned: Shared layout/content templates keep bundled and inline paged output consistent with fewer moving parts.

item.title: HTML5 TOC shows duplicate page number on right
item.justification: On page 1 of the HTML5 table of contents output, the page number appears twice: once in the middle and once on the right. The duplicate right-side page number should be removed so each TOC entry shows a single page number. New evidence shows the duplicate is emitted by paged.js margin content (`div.pagedjs_margin-content`), so the fix must suppress the margin-page number on TOC pages while keeping song page numbers intact.

tasks.task: Reproduce the HTML5 TOC output and trace the paged.js margin boxes that emit div.pagedjs_margin-content on TOC pages.
Identify the CSS/page rule that injects the margin page number and scope it so TOC pages suppress the margin content while song pages retain it.
Update the TOC template or page naming so TOC pages can be targeted by a dedicated @page rule or margin override.
Add or update regression coverage to ensure TOC output has a single page number and margin-content is suppressed on TOC pages.

test.description: HTML5 TOC page-number duplication.
test.assertions: Each TOC entry renders a single page-number element; TOC pages do not emit a right-side pagedjs margin page number.

test.description: Inspect HTML5 print output for page 1 TOC and confirm only one page number is visible.
test.assertions: No pagedjs margin page number appears on TOC pages; song pages still show margin numbers.

risks.risk: Paged.js margin box behavior may vary by browser or paged.js version; scoping rules must avoid hiding page numbers on non-TOC pages.

r.observations: TOC pages now use a named page with a dedicated @page rule that suppresses bottom margin content; HTML5 paged mode falls back to the paged CSS base so page rules are always emitted.
r.lessons-learned: When paged output relies on margin boxes, ensure the paged CSS template is selected even when configs omit paged templates.

item.title: Delegate system: backend-specific handler and config key dispatch

r.observations: Delegate resolution is now backend-aware during Song parsing, so delegate image assets carry backend-specific handler/module/type at creation time while preserving PDF defaults. HTML5 delegate rendering now supports delegate results of type "html", enabling TextBlock and Strum HTML output without attempting PDF XObject handlers. ABC html/html5 handler configuration is implemented via abc2svg_html alias and routed through existing abc2svg engine selection, removing dependency on testing/abc.patch for dispatch.
r.lessons-learned: Backend-specific delegate overrides can be introduced with dotted config keys (e.g. html.handler/html5.handler/pdf.handler) while keeping generic handler defaults for compatibility. When parser-time assets are compared structurally in tests, adding metadata fields such as delegate_type requires explicit expected-structure updates.

item.title: HTML5 delegate SVG rendering: prefer over inline

r.observations: `_render_delegate_result()` for subtype=svg now routes through the HTML5 image pipeline and emits ``. SVG delegate payloads are converted to `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` when provided as inline data, and uri-based SVG still uses the existing `_resolve_image_to_data_uri()` path. No raw delegate `
r.lessons-learned: When assertion intent changes from structural embedding to rendering semantics, update test plans and assertions together to avoid false failure from stale planned test counts. Using the existing render_image/data-URI path for SVG keeps behavior consistent with non-SVG image handling and minimizes maintenance surface.

item.title: Full-test failure: xt/01_config.t cannot find chordpro.prp

r.observations: Root cause was a stale assumption in xt/01_config.t that legacy PRP config (chordpro.prp) is always present. Current repository only ships chordpro.json, so the test aborted before producing TAP. Fix computes config paths from the test file location and skips cleanly when PRP is absent, preserving the parity check when legacy PRP exists. Full-suite verification now passes: standard tests PASS and xt/01_config.t reports SKIP (NOTESTS) without failing make tests.
r.lessons-learned: Extended tests that validate optional/legacy artifacts should gate on artifact presence and report SKIP rather than hard-fail. Using FindBin/File::Spec for absolute path derivation in tests avoids cwd-dependent behavior caused by helper modules that chdir during import.

item.title: HTML5 generation aborts on wide-char SVG delegate base64 encoding

r.observations: Crash root cause was passing UTF-8 flagged SVG text directly to `encode_base64()` in HTML5 delegate SVG rendering. Fix applies an explicit UTF-8 octet boundary (`encode_utf8` when scalar is UTF-8 flagged) before Base64 encoding. User reproduction command now exits successfully (`__EXIT:0`); unknown metadata warnings remain non-fatal parser diagnostics.
r.lessons-learned: When converting text payloads to binary transport encodings (Base64), enforce explicit character-to-octet conversion at the boundary. Mirrored regression suites (`t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t`) should both include new edge-case assertions to keep duplicate test tracks aligned.

item.title: HTML5 SVG img data URI contains wrapper HTML and uses oversized base64 payload

r.observations: Reproduction confirmed original payload defect: decoded SVG data URI began with `<div><svg...`. After fix, generated payloads use `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,` and decode to `<svg...` directly. Reported command now completes successfully and focused regression suites pass.
r.lessons-learned: Delegate payload normalization should enforce format contracts at backend boundaries (e.g., `` with image/svg+xml requires SVG document payload, not arbitrary HTML wrapper markup). For textual SVG payloads, URL-encoded UTF-8 data URIs provide a clear, standards-friendly representation and avoid unnecessary base64 inflation.

item.title: HTML5 diagrams.show:right — vertical stacking layout with direction config option

r.observations: chordpro.json has two html5 { } blocks that are merged last-wins; the diagrams key had to be added to the SECOND block (the one with mode:"print") because the second block overwrites the first entirely. cfgboot.pl must be run directly (perl script/cfgboot.pl) to regenerate Data.pm since `make resources` skips it when Data.pm is newer than chordpro.json. The built-in default config sets html5.diagrams.direction:"vertical", so the direction class IS emitted for the default case (not absent as initially expected in the test).
r.lessons-learned: When chordpro.json has duplicate top-level keys (both html5 { } blocks), JSON::Relaxed uses last-wins and the entire value is replaced — not merged. Any new key must go in the LAST occurrence of the duplicate. Run `perl script/cfgboot.pl <json> -o <Data.pm>` directly rather than `make resources` to force-regenerate Data.pm.

item.title: HTML5 grid strum lines are not rendered as arrow rows

r.observations: `strumline` elements are now rendered by the HTML5 backend instead of being skipped by gridline-only dispatch. Lowercase `|s` strum rows render without bar symbols, while uppercase `|S` (`subtype=cellbars`) keeps bars visible, aligning with documented semantics. Regression tests confirm strum row presence/class and no breakage in existing delegate/diagram behavior.

item.title: HTML5 paired chord/strum grid lines drift out of cell alignment vs PDF

r.observations: HTML5 grid rows now emit deterministic token columns with a shared per-grid `--cp-grid-cols` value, so paired chord/strum rows keep stable horizontal alignment independent of token text width. `chords` tokens are split into per-part rendered cells in HTML5 to align with PDF-style fixed-step progression semantics. Strum rows with lowercase `|s` preserve hidden bar placeholders (`cp-grid-bar-hidden`) so geometry remains synchronized while visual bar suppression behavior is retained.
r.lessons-learned: For visual parity with PDF grids, token stream rendering in HTML5 needs explicit shared column geometry, not per-row content-flow flex layout. Hiding structural tokens via `visibility:hidden` is preferable to dropping nodes when row-to-row alignment matters.

item.title: HTML5 diagrams show:right breaks right-panel box sizing and alignment

r.observations: Right-side diagram layout now uses a dedicated body+diagram wrapper (`cp-song-main-right`) so grid behavior applies only to intended content and no longer entangles title/metadata flow. Right panel containment/alignment is hardened with `justify-self:end`, `width:fit-content`, and bounded diagram container sizing/overflow rules. Template parity was applied to both standard and paged HTML5 song templates, and diagram position regressions now assert the new wrapper and containment rules.
r.lessons-learned: Right-panel layout regressions in HTML5 were driven by applying two-column grid semantics too high in the DOM; isolating layout scope to content blocks improves stability. When HTML5 has standard and paged template variants, structural layout fixes should be mirrored in both to avoid drift.

item.title: Retire deprecated ABC handler alias usage in test paths and stabilize warning-free runs

r.observations: Deprecated module-name ABC handler alias is now canonicalized early (`ChordPro::Delegate::ABC` → `abc2svg`) to preserve backward compatibility without emitting repeated deprecation warnings in normal runs. Page test sequence `t/80_pages.t` through `t/88_pages.t` now explicitly disables user/system config loading (`--no-userconfig --no-sysconfig`) in addition to `--no-default-configs`, removing ambient host-config coupling. `t/83_html5_delegate.t` now asserts that the deprecated ABC warning string is absent, providing regression coverage for warning-free behavior.
r.lessons-learned: Alias canonicalization should happen before warning gates so compatibility paths do not produce avoidable noise. Test invocations that rely on deterministic config behavior should explicitly disable all external config layers, not just defaults.

item.title: HTML5 always passes delegate width for ABC and LilyPond

r.observations: HTML5 delegate dispatch now computes and forwards `pagewidth` for ABC/LilyPond delegates instead of passing undef. Numeric `opts.width` values (including `Npx`) are propagated; otherwise HTML5 uses fallback width 680. Mirrored HTML5 bugfix suites now assert delegate pagewidth forwarding behavior and remain synchronized.
r.lessons-learned: When one backend (PDF) already passes delegate sizing context, matching that contract in HTML5 prevents backend-specific rendering drift. Mirrored test suites should be updated in lockstep for backend regressions to avoid hidden divergence.

item.title: HTML5 ABC multi-image SVG payload collapses to one image and appears to ignore pagewidth

r.observations: HTML5 delegate SVG rendering now detects multi-SVG payloads and emits one `` per SVG block rather than collapsing to the first SVG. This restores full ABC multi-system rendering in HTML5 and removes the false impression that pagewidth is ignored due to dropped systems. Mirrored regression suites now include explicit multi-SVG payload assertions and both pass.
r.lessons-learned: Delegate payload contracts may include compound documents; rendering code should not assume a single root image block. Mirrored test suites remain the safest way to guard against regressions in duplicated bugfix tracks (L-18).

item.title: HTML5 split ABC SVG fragments lose shared style and fallback fonts appear

r.observations: HTML5 now propagates first-fragment SVG style definitions to later split fragments that lack a `<style>` block, preserving class/font rendering consistency. The existing multi-SVG rendering path from item 49 is retained; only style normalization is added before per-fragment image emission. PNG intermediary was considered but intentionally not used due to higher implementation/runtime complexity and vector fidelity loss.
r.lessons-learned: When splitting SVG into multiple image documents, shared CSS must be replicated per fragment because style scope is document-local. A targeted style-propagation step is lower complexity than introducing raster conversion and better preserves output quality.

item.title: HTML5 ABC split fragments with local style still miss shared symbol/font classes

r.observations: Split SVG style normalization now merges shared first-fragment style into all later fragments, including fragments with partial local style blocks. Lowlands verification confirms candidate fragment with local `.f3` plus `slW/sW` usage now contains shared `.slW/.sW` style definitions and notation font-face rules. PNG intermediary was not adopted due to complexity and fidelity/performance trade-offs.
r.lessons-learned: Presence of a local `<style>` block is not sufficient to assume style completeness in split SVG workflows. Merging shared + local style contexts is a practical compromise that preserves vector output quality and avoids raster conversion overhead.

item.title: Refactor HTML5 chord-diagram panel sizing and float behavior for right/top placement
item.justification:
Current HTML5 chord-diagram panel rendering still has coupled layout behaviors across right and top placements: in vertical mode the panel can occupy full available width instead of single-diagram width, and top placement does not consistently let body content flow around the diagram box.
This refactoring isolates panel sizing and placement semantics so layout intent is explicit and behavior-preserving for existing modes: - right + vertical: panel width tracks one chord diagram and remains right-aligned - top: panel participates as a float-like box so song content wraps around it where supported
Related historical fixes (items 38 and 46) addressed stacking direction and wrapper scope; this item focuses on structural CSS/template cleanup to make these rules deterministic and maintainable.

tasks.task: Audit current right/top diagram placement structure in standard and paged song templates and identify where width/stretch behavior is inherited from container rules instead of panel-local rules.

Refactor chord-diagram panel CSS to separate panel sizing from content flow: enforce fit-content/max-content behavior for vertical right placement and explicit right alignment without relying on parent-wide grid stretching.

Refactor top-placement layout so the diagram panel uses float-compatible semantics (or equivalent deterministic flow rule) that allows adjacent song content wrapping while preserving readability and avoiding overlap.
Mirror structural/template changes across standard and paged HTML5 templates to prevent mode drift.
Add/extend regression tests for right+vertical single-diagram-width behavior, right alignment, and top placement content-flow wrapping expectations.
Run focused HTML5 diagram regression suite and confirm no behavior regressions in existing diagram placement cases.

technical-parameters.constraint: Behavior-preserving refactor: no directive/config surface changes and no alteration of diagram SVG payload generation.
Keep compatibility with existing `html5.diagrams.show` and `html5.diagrams.direction` values.
Apply the same structural rules to standard and paged templates.
technical-parameters.pattern: Extract and isolate panel-layout responsibilities from parent wrappers.
Use deterministic width constraints (`fit-content`/equivalent) for vertical right panel sizing.
Prefer CSS-flow semantics over ad-hoc spacing hacks for top placement wrapping.

lessons.lesson: Fixes touching diagram layout must be mirrored across standard+paged templates.
Screen and print outputs should remain visually aligned.
Right-panel stability improves when layout scope is isolated to dedicated wrappers.

test.description: Ensure existing HTML5 diagram bugfix expectations remain intact.
test.assertions: No regressions in previously fixed diagram positioning/containment scenarios.

r.observations: Right-placement stability is improved by forcing the panel to be content-sized at the diagram-container layer (`.cp-chord-diagrams`), not only at the outer wrapper. Top placement now uses a dedicated wrapper with float-based panel flow so body content can wrap beside the diagram box while preserving DOM reading order. Template parity was maintained: both standard and paged song templates now share the same top-wrapper and top-layout class behavior.
r.lessons-learned: Panel sizing constraints must be applied on the element that owns background/border (`.cp-chord-diagrams`), otherwise wrapper-level fit-content rules can still yield full-width visual boxes. When adding a flow-specific layout (top wrap), introducing a dedicated structural wrapper keeps right/top variants isolated and easier to reason about.

item.title: HTML5 strum grid positioning parity options against PDF complex strum layout
item.justification:
The PDF backend handles strum/grid positioning with richer token semantics (barline classes, subtype handling, per-token font choice including `gridstrum`, volta/repeat symbols, and cell-level geometry in `Output/PDF/Grid.pm`).
Current HTML5 implementation improved baseline parity (items 44/45) but still flattens some semantics into CSS classes and token text, which can diverge from PDF positioning for complex strum patterns. We need a planned feature-level parity pass and explicit implementation options so users can choose fidelity vs complexity.

tasks.task: Create a PDF-vs-HTML5 mapping table for strum/grid token classes (`bar`, `repeat1`, `repeat2`, `slash`, `space`, `volta`, `cellbars`) and identify positional mismatches in complex patterns.

Implement chosen parity option in HTML5 grid rendering (`render_gridline` + `_gridline_columns`) so strum token placement follows PDF cell progression rules for multi-token and mixed strum/chord rows.
Update `tab-grid.tt` to align visual semantics with PDF where feasible (bar visibility/placement, repeat/volta positioning, strum glyph spacing) without breaking responsive behavior.
Add focused regression fixtures for complex strum patterns that currently drift from PDF positioning; include lowercase/uppercase strum variants and mixed bar/repeat tokens.
Add mirrored assertions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` plus grid coverage in `t/180_grids.t` to lock parity contract.

technical-parameters.constraint: Do not alter parser token model or PDF rendering behavior; HTML5 must adapt to existing parsed structures.
Maintain backward compatibility for existing HTML5 strum/grid fixtures introduced by items 44 and 45.
No new mandatory runtime dependency; CSS/Perl-only changes.
technical-parameters.nfr: Keep token-to-class mapping centralized in HTML5 backend; avoid scattered symbol-specific CSS hacks.
Complex strum patterns must render deterministically across screen and paged modes.
technical-parameters.pattern: Shared geometry first: compute canonical grid columns per grid block before rendering rows (L-22).
Mirror expectations in duplicated bugfix suites to prevent drift (L-18).
Keep screen and print outputs aligned for review parity (L-7).

implementation-options.option: Minimal parity patch: tune CSS spacing/alignment for `.cp-gridline-strum` and symbol classes only, keeping current token flattening logic. Pros: fast, low risk. Cons: does not fully match PDF for complex mixed tokens.

Renderer-level parity (recommended): enhance HTML5 token pass to mimic PDF cell progression for bars/repeats/strum chords and emit richer class metadata consumed by CSS. Pros: best fidelity/effort balance; robust for complex patterns. Cons: moderate backend + test changes.

High-fidelity semantic port: introduce a dedicated HTML5 grid layout adapter mirroring PDF Grid.pm decision points (including explicit barline/volta anchor semantics). Pros: closest parity. Cons: larger surface area, higher maintenance and regression risk.

entry.note: Implemented Option B renderer-level parity: token/cell metadata + repeat anchor semantics + mirrored tests.
Focused verification PASS on t/180_grids.t, t/html5/09_bugfixes.t, t/190_html5_bugfixes.t (Files=3, Tests=108).

r.observations: Implemented Option B by enhancing HTML5 grid rendering with canonical token/cell progression metadata (`data-token-index`, `data-token-class`, `data-cell-index`, `data-cell-edge`) and repeat anchor semantics (`data-anchor-start`, `data-anchor-end`) for repeat tokens. Added explicit role classes (`cp-grid-token-bar`, `cp-grid-token-cell`) and repeat-anchor styling hooks to support deterministic positioning behavior without changing parser/PDF behavior. Regression coverage was expanded in both mirrored HTML5 bugfix suites and parser-level grid tests to lock repeat-token parsing and HTML metadata contracts. Post-feedback correction: visual impact was initially too weak because shared grid columns were computed from logical cells while rendered token spans also included bars/split chord parts. item.title: HTML5 strum grid misaligns barlines/arrows and misses explicit `~` connector/pause semantics

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use a song containing paired `gridline` + `strumline` rows with mixed bar tokens (`|`, `||`, `|:`, `:|`, `:|:`), repeated `.` placeholders, explicit `~` in strum rows, and multi-symbol chords (e.g. `~A`, `F#m7`, `Bbmaj7`).
Generate HTML5 output (`perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl --generate=HTML5 ...`) and inspect the grid block where strum rows are shown as SVG (`cp-grid-strum-svg`).
Compare chord row and strum row anchors around measure bars and repeat symbols, and compare with PDF output for the same input.

Observe drift: bars/repeat anchors are not consistently stacked between paired rows, strum arrows are not reliably centered under active chord context (including `.` continuation cells), and `~` is not consistently interpreted as arrow-connector (between two arrows) or as short pause spacing (when standalone).

item.expected-result:
In HTML5 strum grids, measure bars/repeat markers must align vertically across chord and strum rows (`|`, `||`, `|:`, `:|`, `:|:`), and strum arrows must align with the active chord unit (including continuation `.` cells).
For strum semantics, `~` must be handled explicitly: - between two direction symbols it connects the two arrow directions as a tight in-beat unit, - standalone (without preceding arrow token) it denotes a short pause with small spacing.
Barlines should be rendered with deterministic music-symbol semantics and continuous vertical stroke appearance across paired chord/strum rows.

analysis.hypothesis: `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm` computes shared rendered columns via `_gridline_layout`, but `render_strumline_svg` currently emits only simple `bar` cells and directional arrow cells. It does not carry bar subtype semantics (`single/double/repeat-start/repeat-end/repeat-both`) into SVG payload, so visual parity with chord-row bar semantics is incomplete.

`ChordPro::Delegate::Strum::strumline_svg` draws every bar as a single `<line>` when `show_bars` is enabled. There is no differentiated drawing for `||`, `|:`, `:|`, `:|:` and no dedicated glyph mapping layer for requested music-symbol variants, causing semantic loss and alignment ambiguity.

In strum rows, dot (`.`) and non-direction tokens currently become empty cells without explicit "active chord continuation" semantics in the rendered output contract. This weakens chord/strum unit coupling for complex rows and contributes to perceived arrow drift under long or split chord tokens.

`~` is currently not represented as a first-class strum semantic token in the HTML5 strum SVG contract. Therefore connector intent (tight link between adjacent arrows) and standalone pause intent (small gap) are lost or flattened into generic spacing.
analysis.root-cause: The current HTML5 strum SVG pathway models bars and strums as minimally typed cells and omits rich barline subtype semantics, continuation-aware anchoring metadata, and explicit `~` connector/pause semantics. As a result, paired chord/strum rows can diverge visually around bars/repeats and cannot guarantee the requested stacked measure + in-beat strum semantics.

tasks.task: Extend HTML5 strum-cell extraction in `render_strumline_svg` to propagate bar subtype metadata (`single`, `double`, `repeat-start`, `repeat-end`, `repeat-both`, `end`) and continuation semantics for `.` cells.

Enhance `ChordPro::Delegate::Strum::strumline_svg` drawing contract to render differentiated barline symbols/geometry for `|`, `||`, `|:`, `:|`, `:|:` (and optionally explicit music-symbol glyph mapping where supported).
Adjust strum arrow anchoring logic so arrows are centered on chord/strum unit columns even when the source token is `.` continuation or split multi-symbol chord groups.
Implement explicit `~` semantics in strum token interpretation: `arrow ~ arrow` = tight connector in the same beat unit; standalone `~` (without preceding arrow) = short pause with reduced spacing.
Update `tab-grid.tt` (and/or SVG spacing rules) so connector and pause spacing are visually stable while preserving deterministic barline continuity across paired lines.

Add mirrored regressions proving bar/repeat stacking parity, arrow-to-chord alignment, and correct `~` connector/pause behavior in complex examples including left/right margin text and multi-symbol chords.

In affected examples, chord names are perceived as not directly above their arrows because the two rows are produced by different rendering surfaces (text-grid vs SVG-grid) with distinct metric behavior.

item.expected-result:
Grid rows with chords and strum arrows should be rendered in one unified SVG surface per grid block (or an equivalent single geometry model), so horizontal anchors are deterministic and chords are visually centered above the corresponding arrows.
The full grid rendering contract should avoid mixed text-grid vs SVG-grid metric drift and preserve existing bar/repeat semantics.

analysis.hypothesis: `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm::render_gridline` renders chord rows as HTML text spans (``), while `render_strumline_svg` renders strum rows as an SVG image (``). The two rendering surfaces are not geometrically unified.

steps-to-reproduce.step: Generate HTML5 output for `testing/lowlands.cho` with `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.

r.summary: Fixed full-grid SVG chord label serialization so chord objects are rendered as readable chord text and no longer leak Perl object stringification artifacts.
r.observations: `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm::grid_block_svg` now resolves `class=chords` part labels via `_chord_display_text` instead of direct scalar interpolation. This removes user-visible artifacts like `ChordPro::Chords::Appearance=ARRAY(...)` from generated `cp-grid-full-svg` payloads. Mirrored regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` now explicitly assert absence of `Appearance=ARRAY(` in decoded full-grid SVG payloads. Verification PASS: `prove -bv t/181_strum_sections.t t/180_grids.t t/html5/09_bugfixes.t t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` (Files=4, Tests=133).
r.lessons-learned: When renderer paths handle mixed token payload types (strings + chord objects), all label emission points must use shared normalization helpers instead of direct string interpolation. Mirrored regression suites are effective to lock bugfix behavior and prevent one-sided test drift in HTML5 rendering changes.

Added bug item 49 via `!run` and auto-approved it (branch: bug/item-49-html5-abc-multi-svg-pagewidth). Root cause: HTML5 delegate SVG path collapsed multi-SVG payloads to the first `<svg>` block, making ABC multi-system output incomplete and masking pagewidth effects. Implemented multi-SVG rendering in `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm` (one IMG per SVG), added mirrored regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t`, rebuilt with `make`, and verified PASS with focused suites (Files=2, Tests=84).

Added bug item 50 via `!run` and auto-approved it (branch: bug/item-50-html5-abc-split-style-propagation). Root cause: split SVG fragments rendered as separate images do not share first-fragment `<style>` definitions, causing fallback fonts in later ABC fragments. Implemented style propagation in `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm` (inject shared style into style-less split fragments), added mirrored regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t`, rebuilt with `make`, and verified PASS with focused suites (Files=2, Tests=88). PNG intermediary path was evaluated and rejected as higher complexity with vector quality trade-offs.

Added bug item 51 via `!run` and auto-approved it (branch: bug/item-51-html5-abc-partial-style-merge). Root cause: partial-style split fragments (with local `.f3`) were skipped by prior propagation logic and still missed shared class/font styles (`.slW/.sW`). Implemented shared-style merge for all later split fragments while preserving local style in `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm`, added mirrored regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t`, rebuilt and verified focused PASS (Files=2, Tests=92), and confirmed on `testing/lowlands-debug.html` that candidate fragment now contains shared style definitions. PNG intermediary path remained rejected due to complexity/fidelity trade-offs.
